A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoA-LoRA work. Their complete main text and Appendices A–C are readable, and text comparison plus rendered-page inspection supports reliable comparison of equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original GLUE accuracy, C4 perplexity, training-time comparisons, zero-shot evaluations and ablation results in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendix C, including the larger-model and rank-sensitivity evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 4.2, Equation (1), corrects the stated LoRA objective: task loss now takes the adapted quantized weights rather than their residual from pretrained weights. This is a limited objective correction; the configuration-aware mapper, Equation (3), and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use C4, the same four GLUE tasks and the same downstream zero-shot tasks. Unseen-configuration and integer mixed-precision evaluation scenarios are also retained unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches within corresponding experiments: QLoRA, LQ-LoRA, Shared-LoRA, GPTQ-LoRA where evaluated, and the plotted full-fine-tuning references. No comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and the appendices retain the same model sizes, adapter ranks, bit-width budgets, accuracy/perplexity/HV metrics, sequence lengths, training epochs and evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: The configuration-search and random-extension ablations, seen/unseen configuration comparisons, rank and segment sensitivity studies, and low-rank correlation analyses are unchanged in Section 5 and Appendix C.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate reporting. Neither reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, plotted results and reported findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 retains CoA-LoRA's accuracy gaps over QLoRA of +4.34%, +8.89%, +1.74% and +7.87% on QNLI, MNLI, SST-2 and QQP.

T1.justification: Equation (1) changes the formal optimization problem by removing the subtraction from pretrained weights inside the task loss. This corrects its mathematical formulation and aligns it with Equation (3). The remaining mathematical definitions and derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about configuration-aware adaptation, Pareto-based search, avoiding repeated fine-tuning and competitive performance.

C2.justification: Result interpretations, mechanism explanations and applicability discussions are unchanged, including explanations of SST-2 generalization and segment sensitivity. Section 3's added qualifiers make an existing distinction explicit without introducing a new limitation or interpretation.

D1.justification: The disclosed mapper architecture, hyperparameters, initialization and configuration-selection procedures, calibration-batch information and implementation URL are unchanged. URL recoloring does not alter access information.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography retain the same cited works and research positioning relative to quantization, LoRA adaptation and adapter-generation methods.

P1.justification: Section 3 adds 'individually' to adapter training and 'shared' to the single-adapter description. Affiliations omit city/country text, and the arXiv version/date marking updates. The document's narrative and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Equation formatting and vertical spacing change on page 5, slightly shifting Figure 4. External URL text changes from cyan to magenta. Figures, table structures, captions and appendix displays otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects Equation (1) to evaluate task loss on adapted quantized weights, resolving an inconsistency with the retained Equation (3) and Algorithm 1. The motivation wording also becomes more precise. These improve correctness and clarity, while the empirical evidence and overall scientific contribution remain unchanged.
